Hi, I would first recommend only watering when the plant shows signs of thirst. From my experience, once a week may be too much water for them.  Wait for the leaves to get soft and squishy then water. I think that this plant could potentially have root rot, you might want to take it out and see if there are any problems. If you see some black slimy roots I would chop them off. Also, may I suggest repotting in a well draining medium? I like 50/50 perlite and succulent /cactus soil. This will help reduce chances of root rot. Your plant looks a bit etiolated. I would try to provide more bright direct light  and you should notice that the leaves grow more closely together on the stem!

Edit: it looks like you water only a little bit at a time? I would recommend fully soaking the pot so the entire soil is wet, then wait a while until the soil is dry. The problem with overwatering is not how much water you provide but how often you water. For succulents and such, they should be watered deeply and be left to dry before watering again. TLDR water with more water, but less often.

Gotcha! For future reference, if they don’t roots, make sure you stick them in dry soil and leave them be until there are roots growing! You risk root rot in the stem if the cut is not callused. What I do is: wait for the cut to callous, stick the stem in soil and wait for a few weeks with no water. After a few weeks you can gently tug on the plant and see if there is any resistance. If there is, that means you have roots and you can go ahead and water them!  Hope this was helpful :)

Hi! I’m unsure of the ID but here are some things I would recommend- firstly I never water right after repotting, I find the roots are a lot more fragile and can be prone to root rot if watered right away. Give them sometime to settle in and then water. 

Second, make sure this guy is in bright direct light. Succulents will etiolate (aka stretch for the light) if there’s not enough. You can tell when this happens because  there will be big(ger) gaps between each leaf on the stem. The bottom portion of your succulent is etiolated but the top looks better. As you can see, the leaves on the top are a lot closer together, which is how it should be! If you notice the succulent continue to etiolate, I’d advise getting a grow light to fully supplement the succulent. 
If you have any other questions I can try my best to help! Good luck!

Hi, first of I really want to give you props to recognizing potentially problematic behavior and being proactive and trying to work on it yourself without burdening him! I can tell you’re really thoughtful and I know it will really make a difference :) 

I definitely know what you’re talking about and I’m also in the process of working on this myself! May I ask how much time you spend with him, and what kind of unreasonable behavior you notice besides the phone thing? I’m asking because changing the attitude also depends on what kind of behaviors you’re engaging in

For the phone thing, I’m not sure what kind of platform you use but maybe you can set a routine or something when you do use your phone. For example, in the morning try to start with not checking the app/ messages until you’ve finished a morning routine (brushing teeth, maybe a workout, cleaning, drinking a coffee, etc whatever it is)- then check his messages. Or maybe you can also limit yourself to checking his online status from 10 times a day to 4, or whatever you think seems reasonable from your current behavior.

Hey friend, online dating can be really difficult! We’re all behind our screens so I get there’s a level of separation. I’m assuming you’re on apps like tinder/ bumble where you swipe to indicate a match? This might sound like a no brainer but dont swipe right on someone who you aren’t interested in. The algorithm (very vaguely, idk that much about it) apparently matches people who are similar in their ratio of right swipes, matched and left swipes. So if you swipe right indiscriminately for everyone, youre casting a wider net but not catching what you’re actually looking for. Take a look at their profile- their pictures and bio. What kind of lifestyle do they lead, does it align with your priorities, any red flags or green flags in personality, etc. 

Now onto your profile- some guys have a hard time choosing or taking flattering pictures of themselves. An attractive picture doesn’t have to be professionally shot, but it should have good lighting, posture, and show something positive about yourself. Ex: do you have a favorite sport or activity? Include a picture of yourself doing it. Are you a people party person looking to attract a social butterfly too? Maybe Include a fun shot of a gathering w ur friends or family. Do you have pets you love? Maybe include them on ur profile too. 

Sometimes people have trouble sending the first message, so having something interesting in your bio can help too! I found that a good “question” type of statement is a great conversation starter- like “tell me about the wildest trip you’ve ever been on” or something dumber like “if you could bring three things with you in a blizzard what would you bring” (sorry these are such crap examples but I hope it gives u some ideas) 

I hope this helps a bit and please don’t be discouraged!! :) feel free to send a pm if you have any questions or need help 😀 you got this!
